newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish growth seen fast after 7.3 pct Q1 GDP rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish growth seen fast after 7.3 pct Q1 GDP rise.

text.p: Poland's economy is expected to continue to grow quickly in the second quarter of 1997 after GDP expanded 7.3 percent in the first quarter, a deputy head of the Central Statistical Office (GUS) said on Friday.

"The Polish economy is not losing momentum...(and) we can assume without much risk that the tempo of GDP growth in the second quarter will again be higher than last year," Janusz Witkowski told a news conference.
In 1996 Poland's gross domestic product (GDP) grew 6.0 percent after a 7.0 percent growth in 1995.

Witkowski said domestic demand remained the main engine of growth in Poland, which increased industrial output by a year-on-year 7.6 percent in the first quarter, on the back of an 11-point jump in manufacturing.
He said firms that produce investment goods grew about year-on-year 18 percent in the first quarter.
Witkowski said companies that produce consumption goods also grew in the first quarter, but not as quickly as in the same period of 1996. He did not give any figures.
Witkowski said that construction output, which increassed 19.5 percent in the first quarter, was a pleasant surpise.

"In this (construction) sector, firms that prepare land for construction grew fastest during the first five months of 1997, which forecasts further quick growth in construction output in the upcomming months or even next year," he said.
He said services grew 6.6 percent in the first quarter.
Witkowski said that agriculture output was less favourable as many crops suffered heavy damage during the winter.
"Generally, the situation in agriculture may be more difficult than last year...but weather conditions could change this," he said.
He said that in the January-May period average wages grew some 5.2 percent in real terms in the industrial sector and about 4.7 percent for pensioners.
